title: World philosophies: Indian, Chinese, Islamic and African metaphysics
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study metaphysics in several world traditions as philosophy, with careful attention to arguments: Indian schools (Nyaya-Vaisheshika realism, Samkhya, Advaita Vedanta, Buddhist no-self and momentariness, and Nagarjuna on emptiness), Chinese philosophy (Daoism, and Confucian and Neo-Confucian metaphysics of li and qi), Islamic philosophy (kalam atomism and occasionalism, al-Ghazali, Avicenna and Mulla Sadra) and African philosophy (personhood and ubuntu), compared with Western views.
primary_reading: Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy: articles on Indian, Chinese, Islamic and African philosophy (free)

weeks.3: Samkhya and Advaita Vedanta: consciousness and Brahman
weeks.4: Buddhist metaphysics: no-self and dependent origination
weeks.6: Nagarjuna: emptiness and the two truths
weeks.7: Daoism: the Dao, change and non-being
weeks.8: Confucian and Neo-Confucian metaphysics: li and qi
weeks.10: Al-Ghazali on causation; Mulla Sadra on the primacy of existence
weeks.11: African philosophy: personhood, community and ubuntu
weeks.12: Comparative metaphysics: what traditions can learn from each other

blocks.deliverable: Compare the Vaisheshika categories with Aristotle's.
Reconstruct the chariot argument for no-self.
Explain the two truths with an example.
Week 7 midterm; compare li and qi with form and matter.
Compare al-Ghazali and Hume on causation.
Write a three-page comparison across two traditions.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Comparative metaphysics paper: write a 2,500-word paper that reconstructs one argument from a non-Western tradition (the Buddhist argument for no-self, Nagarjuna on causation, al-Ghazali on causation, or a Neo-Confucian account of li and qi), sets it beside a Western view of the same question, and evaluates both on their own terms.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
